message.content: {"caption":"Memory examples alongside a line chart comparing task-solving performance with and without ReasoningBank memory.","description":"The figure combines three memory-example panels on the left with a line chart on the right. The “Trajectory Memory” panel shows a sample interaction and reasoning record: navigating to “My Account,” locating “Recent Orders,” using “View All,” and then viewing “My Orders” to find the purchase date. The “Workflow Memory” panel is titled “Retrieve Information from Specific Page Section” and describes a reusable procedure for accessing a specified page section and sending extracted information to the user. The “ReasoningBank Memory” panel contains a “Navigation Strategy” entry, with a description about searching for information in history and content that mentions detecting navigation mode, examining relevant orders, avoiding infinite scroll by using fallbacks, and cross-referencing; the visible text trails off. Small icons identify the three kinds of memory.\n\nThe chart’s horizontal axis is “Number of Tested Tasks” (0–40) and its vertical axis is “Number of Successful Tasks” (0–18). The legend identifies a gray line as “ReasoningBank” and a light-blue line as “No Memory.” Both series generally rise as tested tasks increase; the gray ReasoningBank line stays above the light-blue baseline over the displayed range and finishes higher. Example task annotations and small commerce-related pictograms appear along the plot: “Top-3 best-selling products in Jan 2023,” “Top-2 searches in the store,” “Best-selling product type in Jan 2023,” “Earliest order for customer,” “Num of reviews mentioning ‘decent’,” “Grand total of invoice,” and “Monthly counts of top-3 products for 01/2023-05/2023 in MM:COUNT format.” A red rectangular outline highlights a small icon near the earliest-order annotation. Two red dashed diagonal arrows extend from the chart area toward the upper-left and lower-left, with no visible labels.
